subject: Hightower Ops - tenant log retention exception & SIG/CAIQ evidence
messages:
From: Sarah Li <sarah.li@hightowerops.com>
To: chloe.martin@redwood.ai
Cc: tom.reynolds@hightowerops.com
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hightower Ops - tenant log retention exception & SIG/CAIQ evidence

Hi Chloe,

Thanks for taking the call yesterday. Hightower is evaluating Redwood for an internal audit and we have one outstanding requirement from Compliance: we need a tenant-scoped debug/audit log retention window of 90 days for a specific integration namespace.

From what I understand your platform default for debug-level tenant logs is 30 days. Before we escalate to procurement/legal, can you confirm:
- Whether you support a customer-scoped retention override for a single tenant (not org-wide).
- What evidence you can provide for SOC 2 / SIG / CAIQ specifically tied to retention and proof-of-delete (redacted reports are fine).
- Any limitations around audit exports or on-demand bulk exports for forensic requests.

I attached a short spreadsheet with the audit requirements columned by our internal controls. We’d like to know if this is achievable and what the path to an exception or contract addendum looks like.

Appreciate a quick read — we are trying to get this surfaced to our security committee by next week.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Li
Security Program Manager | Hightower Ops
attachments: Hightower_SAR_requirements.xlsx

From: chloe.martin@redwood.ai
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@hightowerops.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hightower Ops - tenant log retention exception & SIG/CAIQ evidence

Sarah — thanks for the clear note and the spreadsheet. Short answer: we can support a tenant-specific retention extension for debug/audit traces, but it requires a scoped addendum (retention override) and a short implementation window to enable longer TTL and controlled storage.

Next steps I propose:
1) Priyom, can you confirm what evidence artifacts we can share (SOC2, CAIQ answers, proof-of-delete descriptions)?
2) I’ll put together an exception addendum draft and a proposed timeline for enabling a 90-day TTL for the named tenant.
3) If Hightower Legal wants a quick redline, we can route through our legal counsel and propose a DocuSign path.

Ben — looping you in for commercial implications (pricing delta for longer retention, and any SLA notes).

Sarah — I’ll aim to get a preliminary evidence packet and the addendum draft to you by EOD Monday.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Senior Sales Manager
Redwood Inference

From: priyom.das@redwood.ai
To: chloe.martin@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hightower Ops - tenant log retention exception & SIG/CAIQ evidence

Chloe / Ben — technical confirmation and catalog of artifacts we can provide:

1) Configuration: We support tenant-scoped retention overrides, implemented as a per-tenant policy attached to the telemetry namespace. It persists to our configuration service and triggers storage tier rules. Implementation requires a short maintenance window (typically < 2 business days) to provision the storage class and adjust lifecycle policies.

2) Proof/evidence we can attach (redacted where necessary):
- Redwood SOC 2 Type II report (summary redacted) — redact PII, provide scope page and control mapping. (attached: redwood-soc2-2026-redacted.pdf)
- SIG/CAIQ responses: We maintain a CAIQ/Q&A pack that maps retention and proof-of-delete controls to our operational procedures. (attached: caIQ-summary-answers.docx)
- Proof-of-delete flow: sequence diagrams and retention lifecycle description + sample audit export commands.
- Demo-ready audit export: we can run a tenant export (CSV) on request for a short-lived forensic snapshot.

3) Limitations / notes:
- Increasing the retention window increases storage costs — commercial team will need to approve pricing adjustment (Ben).
- For proof-of-delete, we can produce a signed export and a deletion confirmation that includes storage object IDs and deletion timestamps, but we cannot provide raw customer data in reports (must be requested via SAR process).

I’ll bundle the artifacts into an evidence packet and include an ops-runbook for on-demand exports.

Attachments: redwood-soc2-2026-redacted.pdf, caIQ-summary-answers.docx, retention-addendum-template.docx

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Staff Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: chloe.martin@redwood.ai
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@hightowerops.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@hightowerops.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 12:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hightower Ops - tenant log retention exception & SIG/CAIQ evidence

Hi Sarah / Tom — attached is the preliminary evidence packet and a draft retention addendum. Quick notes:
- Evidence packet (RDW_evidence_packet_v1.zip) includes the redacted SOC2 summary, CAIQ Q&A mapping for retention, and an ops-runbook for exports and proof-of-delete.
- Retention addendum (retention-addendum-draft.docx) proposes: 90-day tenant-scoped debug retention for namespace 'hightower-integration', a 7-day rollback window, and billing for incremental storage at a discounted rate for committed volume.
- DocuSign link (below) is a placeholder; we can route to Legal once Hightower confirms redlines.

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/link/EXAMPLE-12345

Would you like a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the attestation artifacts? If so, Ben and Priyom can join to cover pricing and security details.

Best,
Chloe
Senior Sales Manager
Redwood Inference
attachments: RDW_evidence_packet_v1.zip, retention-addendum-draft.docx

From: Hightower Legal <legal@hightowerops.com>
To: chloe.martin@redwood.ai
Cc: Sarah Li <sarah.li@hightowerops.com>, tom.reynolds@hightowerops.com
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hightower Ops - tenant log retention exception & SIG/CAIQ evidence

Chloe — thanks for the packet. A few quick redline items from Legal:
1) We need explicit language about retention scope limiting to a single named tenant and an assurance that no cross-tenant rehydration will occur.
2) Request sample audit export format (headers & a 1-row example) to confirm it contains the metadata our auditors expect.
3) Can you confirm whether retained debug logs include any application-level PII by default? If yes, we’ll need a redaction option or scoped pseudonymization.

We are available for a short call tomorrow 10:00–11:00 PT to finalize redlines. Please loop in your legal counsel or confirm Redwood lapses to standard addendum language.

Tom Reynolds
Sr. Counsel, Hightower Ops
